title: Sinlessness of Christ
definition: The sinlessness of Christ is the doctrine that Jesus never sinned in thought, word, desire, or deed.
summary: Jesus lived in perfect holiness and obedience, making Him the spotless Savior sinners need.
christFocus: Jesus' sinless life qualified Him to offer Himself as the spotless sacrifice for sin and to provide perfect righteousness for His people.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Jesus Christ was tempted, yet He never sinned. His obedience was not partial or outward only. He was holy in thought, desire, word, action, love, worship, and submission to the Father.

His sinlessness matters because sinners need more than a teacher. They need a spotless substitute. If Christ had sin of His own, He could not bear the sins of others. But because He is without sin, He is the acceptable sacrifice and the righteous representative of His people.

The sinlessness of Christ also reveals the beauty of true humanity. Jesus shows what perfect obedience, love, humility, courage, and holiness look like before God.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Many people excuse sin as unavoidable or define righteousness by comparison with others. The sinlessness of Christ exposes the seriousness of sin while also giving hope because the Savior has obeyed where sinners have failed.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Do not hide your sin from the sinless Savior. Confess it, trust His cleansing, and look to His obedience as your hope. Follow His example by resisting temptation through Scripture, prayer, dependence on the Father, and obedience.
